You are a dependency vulnerability triage agent. You receive the parsed contents of one dependency file: the dependencies whose exact versions are known, and the entries that could not be checked.

Tools:
- check_packages: known vulnerabilities per exact package version (OSV), with CISA KEV status and EPSS.
- get_vulnerability: NVD details for one vulnerability. Slow (rate limited); use it only when you need details.

Process:
1. Call check_packages once with every entry under "dependencies", using ecosystem, name and version exactly as given.
2. If you need details for a few vulnerabilities, call get_vulnerability for those only.
3. Return the final report as JSON that follows the response schema.

Report rules:
- Grounding: list only vulnerabilities returned by check_packages, and use the tool's `id` field as the id. Never add vulnerabilities from memory. Suspicions the tools cannot confirm (for example vulnerable transitive dependencies) go in `notes`, never in `packages`.
- Completeness: include every vulnerability the tool returned for every vulnerable package, including low-priority ones.
- Ranking: rank 1 is the most urgent; ranks are unique across the whole report. Every CISA KEV-listed vulnerability ranks above every vulnerability that is not KEV-listed. Within each group, higher EPSS ranks higher; use severity to break ties.
- kev: true only if the tool's `kev` field for that vulnerability is an object (listed), otherwise false.
- upgrade_to (per package): the lowest version that fixes ALL of that package's vulnerabilities, not only the most urgent one. Choose it from the fixed versions the tool returned for that package. Fixed versions often belong to different release lines (for example 2.3.1 / 2.12.2 / 2.15.0 for three branches); the version you choose must not be affected by any of the package's vulnerabilities and must not be lower than the installed version. Use null when no single version fixes all of them, and say why in `reason`.
- A vulnerability with `last_affected` affects versions up to and including that version; versions above it are not affected by it, so it does not stop you from choosing a higher fixed version.
- The same vulnerability id can affect two packages; list it under each affected package.
- unchecked: repeat every entry of the input "unchecked" list with its reason, plus anything else you could not check.
- Do not list packages that have no vulnerabilities.
- Write `summary`, `reason` and `notes` in Korean.

CISA KEV 등재 항목은 없으며, 순위는 EPSS와 심각도 기준입니다. spring-context 3.2.6과 hibernate-core 4.3.7은 오래된 메이저 라인이라 업그레이드 폭이 큽니다. 취약점이 없다고 나온 패키지도 OSV 결과일 뿐 안전이 증명된 것은 아닙니다. 전이 의존성은 확인하지 않았습니다.","packages":[{"package":"Maven/org.springframework:spring-context@3.2.6.RELEASE","upgrade_to":"6.1.20","reason":"세 취약점을 모두 해소하는 최소 버전은 6.1.20입니다. CVE-2025-22233은 5.3.39와 6.0.23까지 영향을 받고 6.1.20에서 수정됩니다. 5.x 라인에는 도구가 반환한 수정 버전이 없어 모두 해소할 수 없으므로 6.x 라인이 필요합니다. 같은 Spring 버전을 쓰는 spring-orm, spring-aspects, spring-test도 함께 올리는 것이 좋습니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2022-22968","rank":1,"priority":"high","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2024-38820","rank":6,"priority":"medium","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2025-22233","rank":7,"priority":"low","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/org.hsqldb:hsqldb@2.3.2","upgrade_to":"2.7.1","reason":"CVE-2022-41853(원격 코드 실행, CVSS 9.8)의 수정 버전인 2.7.1로 올리면 됩니다. 이 패키지의 취약점은 이 하나뿐입니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2022-41853","rank":2,"priority":"critical","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/org.hibernate:hibernate-core@4.3.7.Final","upgrade_to":"5.3.20.Final","reason":"CVE-2019-14900은 5.3.18 이상에서, CVE-2020-25638은 5.3.20.Final 이상에서 수정되므로 5.3.20.Final이 두 취약점을 모두 해소하는 가장 낮은 버전입니다. 4.x에서 5.x로의 메이저 업그레이드이므로 API 호환성 검토가 필요합니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2020-25638","rank":3,"priority":"high","kev":false},{"id":"CVE-2019-14900","rank":4,"priority":"medium","kev":false}]},{"package":"Maven/junit:junit@4.12","upgrade_to":"4.13.1","reason":"CVE-2020-15250의 수정 버전인 4.13.1로 올리면 됩니다. 테스트 scope 의존성입니다.","vulnerabilities":[{"id":"CVE-2020-15250","rank":5,"priority":"medium","kev":false}]}],"unchecked":[],"notes":["CISA KEV 등재 취약점은 없습니다.","spring-orm, spring-aspects, spring-test(3.2.6.RELEASE)와 hibernate-entitymanager(4.3.7.Final), cglib, aspectjweaver, c3p0, commons-collections, hibernate-jpa-2.0-api는 OSV에서 알려진 취약점이 없다고 반환되었습니다. 이는 안전하다는 증명이 아니므로 spring-context, hibernate-core와 함께 버전을 맞춰 점검하는 것이 좋습니다.","전이 의존성은 확인하지 않았습니다. 해결된 의존성 트리(mvn dependency:tree 등)를 기준으로 추가 점검이 필요합니다.","부모 POM(io.github.snyk:todolist-mvc:0.0.1-SNAPSHOT)의 속성과 관리 버전이 적용된 상태로 분석했습니다.","spring-context 3.2.6과 hibernate-core 4.3.7은 지원이 끝난 오래된 라인이므로, 취약점 외에도 장기적인 업그레이드 계획이 필요합니다."]}
thinking:
Nothing is known to be exploited in the wild, so I'm ranking the Spring findings by EPSS score within the non-KEV group. The spring-context 3.2.6 entries are next, with CVE-2022-22968 at the highest EPSS and a HIGH rating, followed by CVE-2024-38820 and CVE-2025-22233.

I'm checking which fixed version covers every CVE on spring-context, since the 5.x releases don't seem to clear CVE-2024-38820. The tool's fixed list tops out at 6.2.7, so I'm weighing 6.1.20 as the likely upgrade target, since it sits above the 5.3.19 fix and the 6.1.14 fix for the newer CVE.

I'm settling on 6.1.20 as the upgrade target for spring-context: 6.x sits above the 5.3.19 fix for CVE-2022-22968, and 6.1.20 covers the 6.1.14 fix for CVE-2024-38820 as well as CVE-2025-22233, which only gets fixed there. I also want to note that the other 3.2.6 Spring modules (spring-orm, spring-aspects, spring-test) show no known vulns in OSV, but they should be moved to the same version as spring-context.

I'm checking whether hibernate-core 4.3.7.Final can reach a single fix version for both CVEs, and 5.3.20.Final clears the 5.3.18 fix for CVE-2019-14900 and the 5.3.20.Final fix for CVE-2020-25638, so that looks like the lowest option.

I'm settling on 5.3.20.Final for hibernate-core, since it clears both the 5.3.18 fix for CVE-2019-14900 and the 5.3.20 fix for CVE-2020-25638, and 5.3.18 alone would leave the second one open. Next I'm moving on to junit, where CVE-2020-15250 is fixed in 4.13.1.

I'm ordering the findings by EPSS now, with CVE-2022-22968 on spring-context at the top, followed by the hsqldb CVE, the two hibernate-core CVEs, junit, and the two remaining spring-context CVEs at the bottom.

I'm setting priorities by severity label: hsqldb's CVE-2022-41853 is critical, CVE-2022-22968 and CVE-2020-25638 are high, and the rest are medium or low. Ranking by EPSS still puts CVE-2022-22968 first and the hsqldb CVE second, and the two hibernate-core entries come third and fourth.

I'm noting that the other Spring modules (orm, aspects, test) need to move to the same version as spring-context, even though OSV lists no vulns for them. I'm also considering that the parent POM properties were applied and that transitive dependencies weren't checked. I'm limiting the final list to the packages with vulnerabilities: spring-context, hsqldb, hibernate-core, and junit.

I'm settling the package string format as ecosystem/name@installed_version, and for spring-context I'm confirming that 6.1.20 covers all three CVEs, since the 5.x line has no returned fix for CVE-2024-38820.

I'm confirming that 6.1.20 clears every spring-context CVE, since 6.1.14 covers the 2024 one and 6.1.20 the 2025 one. For hibernate-core, 5.3.20.Final clears both the 5.3.18 and 5.3.20 fixes, so I'll note that moving from 4.3 to 5.3 is a large jump with API changes.
